articles.title: ‘Parkinson’s Valley’: the herbicide haunting a New York farm town
articles.description: Paraquat is banned in over 70 countries. Some farmers and their families in Hebron believe the pesticide is causing Parkinson’s disease and are demanding that New York ban it Gordon Chaplin gingerly stepped out of the car at the top of the steep hill behind his farmhouse, sporting a bandage on his hand from a fall the day before. He gripped his cane as he shuffled through the knee-high grass. He stopped every few feet to catch his breath, leaning on his caregiver for support. Looking out at the distant Adirondacks and Catskill mountains, he thought back to the years when he could run up the hill with ease. Continue reading...

articles.title: Penguins and dolphins among nearly 400 Australian species under threat from bird flu as ‘true extent of disaster’ revealed
articles.description: Assessment of more than 2,000 native species warns nearly one in five at high risk of deadly H5N1, including parrots, fur seals and quolls Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Almost 400 native Australian bird and mammal species have been assessed as being at a high risk – or worse – from the deadly H5N1 bird flu virus, a federal government assessment has revealed. Some of Australia’s most beloved animals – including species of penguins, fur seals, quolls, dolphins, more than 300 birds and the Tasmanian devil – are considered at least high risk from the virus, meaning they could suffer “severe reduction in population size or viability” or worse if it reached them. articles.title: WALANG PASOK: Almost all Pangasinan LGUs suspend classes due to Maymay
articles.description: CALASIAO, Pangasinan – With Pangasinan placed under tropical cyclone wind signals, 43 towns and four cities suspended face-to-face classes in both public and private schools on Wednesday (August 4). Three northwestern Pangasinan towns were placed under Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2, while the rest of the province remained under Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 due to Tropical Storm Maymay (international name: Kujira).
